Synopsis:
    The Indian rupee is under significant pressure from a sharp oil price rally (Brent +12% on the week, near $110/bbl) driven by intensifying Middle East shipping route disruptions. The RBI, having previously supported the rupee to a two-month high of 94.30, is showing reluctance to aggressively defend the currency. Rising U.S. Treasury yields (~5% on 10Y), fuelled by strong PPI data and ~70% market-implied probability of a Fed rate hike, compound the pressure. India's heavy oil import dependency amplifies the macro risk to its external balances, growth and inflation.
